---
title: "TERRE GRS: Epigenome-wide asssociation analysis"
output: html_notebook
---

The manuscript "A Parkinson’s disease genetic risk score associates with blood DNAm on chromosome 17" explores how a genetic risk score (GRS) for Parkinson's disease (PD) associates with blood DNA methylation in the TERRE study of French agricultural workers, and evaluates GRS associations with DNAm in each sex as well as their sensitivity to non-genetic factors. This was originally spearheaded by Will Casazza and was posted as a pre-print on medRxiv in 2023. The current revision (2024, led by Sam Schaffner) aims to address previous reviewer feedback and prepare the manuscript for re-submission.


In this script, EWAS is conducted to identify DNAm patterns associated with the GRS in the cross-sex and sex-stratified samples in TERRE. The models are adjusted for batch, cell type, and disease status. Results will be compared with the previous models (adjusted for 10 DNAm PCs).


Last updated Nov 15, 2025 by Samantha Schaffner: using 83-SNP GRS.

Based on code by Will Casazza

# Association analysis

## EWAS model checks

Prior to looking at results, I'll assess whether the new EWAS model seems appropriate using three measures:

*1. Variance inflation factor*: The variance inflation factor (VIF) can be used to detect collinearity. Higher VIF values indicate a greater degree of collinearity. Typically VIF < 5 is considered acceptable.


*2. Q-Q plot of nominal p-values*: If the variable of interest does not affect global DNAm, p-values should distribute close to the center line on a normal Q-Q plot, with some deviation at the tail indicating associations detected. The shape of the Q-Q plot can visually indicate model inflation or deflation.


*3. Bias and inflation calculations*: The "bacon" package (van Iterson et al., 2017) was developed to calculate and optionally, correct for, bias and inflation observed in epigenome-wide association studies. It models test statistics using a Bayesian mixture model, and estimates the model parameters: bias (mean) and inflation (standard deviation). The Bayesian mixture model is proposed to more accurately model the quantitative nature and technical/biological influences on epigenomic and transcriptomic data, as opposed to the traditional genomic inflation factor (based on discrete genotypes).


```{r ewas models, eval=F}
## Preparing data
# match meta data and M-values
meta <- meta[complete.cases(meta$CTP_PC1),]
mvals <- mvals[,match(meta$patient, colnames(mvals))]
all(colnames(mvals)==meta$patient) #TRUE

# subset meta data to relevant columns and re-format
meta_sub <- meta[,c("patient","GRS_scaled","SCORE1_AVG","PD","age","sex","geno_V3","geno_V4","geno_V5","CTP_PC1","CTP_PC2","CTP_PC3","CTP_PC4","CTP_PC5","CTP_PC6","smoking","pesticides","head_trauma","alcohol1","levodopa","agonist","plate","SentrixPosition_A")]
str(meta_sub)
meta_sub$PD <- as.factor(meta_sub$PD)
meta_sub$sex <- as.factor(meta_sub$sex)
meta_sub$smoking <- as.factor(meta_sub$smoking)
meta_sub$pesticides <- as.factor(meta_sub$pesticides)
meta_sub$head_trauma <- as.factor(meta_sub$head_trauma)
meta_sub$alcohol1 <- as.factor(meta_sub$alcohol1)
meta_sub$levodopa <- as.factor(meta_sub$levodopa)
meta_sub$plate <- as.factor(meta_sub$plate)
meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A <- as.factor(meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A)

## Variance inflation factor
# check for one CpG (result is the same as when applied to all CpGs and averaged)
vif(lm(mvals[1,] ~ meta_sub$GRS_scaled + meta_sub$age + meta_sub$sex + meta_sub$geno_V3 + meta_sub$geno_V4 + meta_sub$geno_V5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC1 + meta_sub$CTP_PC2 + meta_sub$CTP_PC3 + meta_sub$CTP_PC4 + meta_sub$CTP_PC5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC6 + meta_sub$plate + meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A + meta_sub$PD))[,3]
#       meta_sub$GRS_scaled               meta_sub$age               meta_sub$sex           meta_sub$geno_V3           meta_sub$geno_V4           meta_sub$geno_V5 
#                  1.042602                   1.109200                   1.541326                   1.085064                   1.101569                   1.061150 
#          meta_sub$CTP_PC1           meta_sub$CTP_PC2           meta_sub$CTP_PC3           meta_sub$CTP_PC4           meta_sub$CTP_PC5           meta_sub$CTP_PC6 
#                  1.096277                   1.130351                   1.316783                   1.141944                   1.244352                   1.159645 
#            meta_sub$plate meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A                meta_sub$PD 
#                  1.135184                   1.051294                   1.073484


## Q-Q plot
#scaled GRS
pvals <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals[x,] ~ meta_sub$GRS_scaled + meta_sub$age + meta_sub$sex + meta_sub$geno_V3 + meta_sub$geno_V4 + meta_sub$geno_V5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC1 + meta_sub$CTP_PC2 + meta_sub$CTP_PC3 + meta_sub$CTP_PC4 + meta_sub$CTP_PC5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC6 + meta_sub$plate + meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A + meta_sub$PD)))[2,4]
   }) #runtime ~1 hour
qqunif.plot(pvals, title="Model adjusted for PD, batch, and cell type")

## Bias and inflation (based on Z-values)
zvals <- qnorm(pvals)
bacon(zvals)
#...estimated bias: -0.27.
#...estimated inflation: 1.

#non-scaled GRS
pvals_orig <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals[x,] ~ meta_sub$SCORE1_AVG + meta_sub$age + meta_sub$sex + meta_sub$geno_V3 + meta_sub$geno_V4 + meta_sub$geno_V5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC1 + meta_sub$CTP_PC2 + meta_sub$CTP_PC3 + meta_sub$CTP_PC4 + meta_sub$CTP_PC5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC6 + meta_sub$plate + meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A + meta_sub$PD)))[2,4]
   })
qqunif.plot(pvals_orig, title="Model adjusted for PD, batch, and cell type")

## Bias and inflation (based on Z-values)
zvals <- qnorm(pvals_orig)
bacon(zvals)
#...estimated bias: -0.27.
#...estimated inflation: 1.

### Model is biased, regardless of whether new GRS is scaled.
```
![Q-Q plot for updated EWAS model](/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/qqplot_grs_scaled_16Nov2025.png)

The model with the 83-SNP GRS is biased according to the shifted distribution observed on the Q-Q plot, and when compared with the empirical null using bacon. Next, let's check the meta data correlation heat map and loadings of the variables onto DNAm PCs, to give clues how to optimize the model.

## Meta data correlation heat map
```{r meta heat, eval=F}
source("~/kobor_shared_coding_resource/PCA_Plot_Function.R")
source("~/kobor_shared_coding_resource/correlation_pval.R")

#Create correlation matrix
terre_meta_cor <- meta_sub[,-(c(1,3))] #remove "patient" and non-scaled GRS
cormat <- correlation_pval(terre_meta_cor)

# Get lower triangle of the correlation matrix
get_lower_tri<-function(cormat){
    cormat[upper.tri(cormat)] <- NA
    return(cormat)
  }
# Get upper triangle of the correlation matrix
get_upper_tri <- function(cormat){
    cormat[lower.tri(cormat)]<- NA
    return(cormat)
  }

upper_tri <- get_upper_tri(cormat)

#colour if sig
for(x in 1:nrow(upper_tri)){
  for(y in 1:ncol(upper_tri)){
    if(is.na(upper_tri[x,y])==FALSE){
    if(as.numeric(upper_tri[x,y])<=0.001){upper_tri[x,y]<-"<=0.001"}else{
    if(as.numeric(upper_tri[x,y])<=0.01){upper_tri[x,y]<-"<=0.01"}else{
      if(as.numeric(upper_tri[x,y])<=0.05){upper_tri[x,y]<-"<=0.05"}else{upper_tri[x,y]<-">0.05"}}}}
  }}
melted_cormat <- reshape2::melt(upper_tri, na.rm = TRUE)
png("~/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/terre_meta_cor.png", width=600, height=600)
ggplot(data = melted_cormat, aes(Var2, Var1, fill = value))+
 geom_tile(color = "white")+
scale_fill_manual(values=c("#084594","#4292c6","#9ecae1","#deebf7"), name="p-value") +
  theme_minimal()+ 
 theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, 
    size = 12, hjust = 1))+
 coord_fixed()
dev.off()
```
![Meta data correlation heat map](/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/terre_meta_cor.png)

Sex is correlated strongly with cell type, smoking, pesticide exposure, and alcohol intake.

Row is correlated strongly with cell type PC5.

The GRS correlates moderately with PD status.

## Sex stratification

While there is not expected to be a strong "tail" on the Q-Q plot due to lack of association between the GRS and DNAm PCs, let's aim to reduce the model bias and see if any associations are detectable. As males and females have very different exposure levels, we will start by sex-stratifying the data.

```{r sex strat, eval=F}
#### sex stratification
ncol(mvals_F <- mvals[,colnames(mvals) %in% meta_sub[meta_sub$sex=="F","patient"]]) #100
nrow(meta_F <- meta_sub[match(colnames(mvals_F),meta_sub$patient),]) #100
ncol(mvals_M <- mvals[,colnames(mvals) %in% meta_sub[meta_sub$sex=="M","patient"]]) #118
nrow(meta_M <- meta_sub[match(colnames(mvals_M),meta_sub$patient),]) #118

# PCA females
rownames(meta_F) <- meta_F$patient
meta_categorical <- meta_F[,c("PD","smoking","pesticides","head_trauma","alcohol1","levodopa","agonist","plate","SentrixPosition_A")]
meta_continuous <- meta_F[,c("GRS_scaled","age","geno_V3","geno_V4","geno_V5","CTP_PC1","CTP_PC2","CTP_PC3","CTP_PC4","CTP_PC5")]
ord <- c(seq(1:(ncol(meta_categorical)+ncol(meta_continuous))))
all.equal(colnames(mvals_F), rownames(meta_categorical)) #TRUE

#PCA on M-values: input
PCA_full<-princomp(mvals_F[complete.cases(mvals_F),])
PCA_Plot(PCA_full, type="sparse", MTC=T, Discrete=T)

#females
pvals_F <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals_F), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals_F[x,] ~ meta_F$GRS_scaled + meta_F$age + meta_F$geno_V3 + meta_F$geno_V4 + meta_F$geno_V5 + meta_F$CTP_PC1 + meta_F$CTP_PC2 + meta_F$CTP_PC3 + meta_F$CTP_PC4 + meta_F$CTP_PC5 + meta_F$CTP_PC6 + meta_F$plate + meta_F$SentrixPosition_A + meta_F$PD)))[2,4]

qqunif.plot(pvals_F, title="Females model")

meta_continuous <- meta_M[,c("GRS_scaled","age","geno_V3","geno_V4","geno_V5","CTP_PC1","CTP_PC2","CTP_PC3","CTP_PC4","CTP_PC5")]

PCA_Plot(PCA_full, type="sparse", MTC=T, Discrete=T)

pvals_M <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals_M), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals_M[x,] ~ meta_M$GRS_scaled + meta_M$age + meta_M$geno_V3 + meta_M$geno_V4 + meta_M$geno_V5 + meta_M$CTP_PC1 + meta_M$CTP_PC2 + meta_M$CTP_PC3 + meta_M$CTP_PC4 + meta_M$CTP_PC5 + meta_M$CTP_PC6 + meta_M$plate + meta_M$SentrixPosition_A + meta_M$PD)))[2,4]
```

## Males-only model optimization

Next let's try adjusting for head trauma in the male-only model to see if it improves bias.

```{r male ht, eval=F}
vif(lm(mvals_M[1,] ~ meta_M$GRS_scaled + meta_M$age + meta_M$head_trauma + meta_M$geno_V3 + meta_M$geno_V4 + meta_M$geno_V5 + meta_M$CTP_PC1 + meta_M$CTP_PC2 + meta_M$CTP_PC3 + meta_M$CTP_PC4 + meta_M$CTP_PC5 + meta_M$CTP_PC6 + meta_M$plate + meta_M$SentrixPosition_A + meta_M$PD))[,3]
#       meta_M$GRS_scaled               meta_M$age       meta_M$head_trauma           meta_M$geno_V3 
#                1.054797                 1.165156                 1.109223                 1.130007 
#          meta_M$geno_V4           meta_M$geno_V5           meta_M$CTP_PC1           meta_M$CTP_PC2 
#                1.130977                 1.157928                 1.154730                 1.182198 
#          meta_M$CTP_PC3           meta_M$CTP_PC4           meta_M$CTP_PC5           meta_M$CTP_PC6 
#                1.191569                 1.238024                 1.301678                 1.124866 
#            meta_M$plate meta_M$SentrixPosition_A                meta_M$PD 
#                1.131692                 1.106613                 1.164631 

pvals_M <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals_M), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals_M[x,] ~ meta_M$GRS_scaled + meta_M$age + meta_M$geno_V3 + meta_M$geno_V4 + meta_M$geno_V5 + meta_M$CTP_PC1 + meta_M$CTP_PC2 + meta_M$CTP_PC3 + meta_M$CTP_PC4 + meta_M$CTP_PC5 + meta_M$CTP_PC6 + meta_M$plate + meta_M$SentrixPosition_A + meta_M$PD + meta_M$head_trauma)))[2,4]
   })
png("~/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/qqplot_ht_M.png")
qqunif.plot(pvals_M, title="Males model, adjusted for head trauma")
dev.off()

## Bias and inflation (based on Z-values)
zvals <- qnorm(pvals_M)
bacon(zvals)
#...estimated bias: -0.31.
#...estimated inflation: 1.
```
![Head trauma-adjusted model](/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/qqplot_ht_M.png)

This slightly reduces bias.

Next, adjust for smoking and alcohol consumption, as done in the previous TERRE npj PD paper.

```{r male ht alc smoke, eval=F}
pvals_M <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals_M), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals_M[x,] ~ meta_M$GRS_scaled + meta_M$age + meta_M$geno_V3 + meta_M$geno_V4 + meta_M$geno_V5 + meta_M$CTP_PC1 + meta_M$CTP_PC2 + meta_M$CTP_PC3 + meta_M$CTP_PC4 + meta_M$CTP_PC5 + meta_M$CTP_PC6 + meta_M$plate + meta_M$SentrixPosition_A + meta_M$PD + meta_M$head_trauma + meta_M$alcohol1 + meta_M$smoking)))[2,4]
```

![Head trauma, smoking, and alcohol-adjusted model](/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/qqplot_ht_smoke_alc_M.png)

Adjusting for smoking and alcohol further improved bias and the Q-Q plot.

# Propensity matching

The MatchIt package can be used to weight treatment and control groups such that the biasing effects of covariate imbalances are reduced.

### Cross-sex
```{r MatchIt, eval=F}
library(MatchIt)

# Check initial imbalances
#create a matchit object relating the treatment to the covariates

### Treatment must be binary! Split by the median of the GRS.
summary(meta_sub$GRS_scaled)
#     Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max. 
#-2.347875 -0.643047 -0.074174 -0.001345  0.691074  2.826025 

meta_sub$GRS_above_med <- (meta_sub$GRS_scaled > median(meta_sub$GRS_scaled))
summary(meta_sub$GRS_above_med)
#   Mode   FALSE    TRUE 
#logical     109     109 

cross.out0 <- summary(matchit(GRS_above_med ~ age + alcohol1 + smoking + head_trauma, data = meta_sub,
                 method = NULL, distance = "glm"))$sum.all

cross.out0
#             Means Treated Means Control Std. Mean Diff. Var. Ratio   eCDF Mean    eCDF Max Std. Pair Dist.
#distance         0.5082936    0.49170638      0.26171314  0.9477532 0.072455729 0.165137615              NA
#age             67.0865123   66.76623401      0.05495052  0.6691645 0.033208425 0.100917431              NA
#alcohol11        0.1467890    0.19266055     -0.12961896         NA 0.045871560 0.045871560              NA
#alcohol12        0.3669725    0.32110092      0.09517337         NA 0.045871560 0.045871560              NA
#alcohol13        0.0733945    0.11009174     -0.14071951         NA 0.036697248 0.036697248              NA
#alcohol14        0.4128440    0.37614679      0.07453560         NA 0.036697248 0.036697248              NA
#smoking1         0.6788991    0.72477064     -0.09824719         NA 0.045871560 0.045871560              NA
#smoking2         0.2477064    0.21100917      0.08501023         NA 0.036697248 0.036697248              NA
#smoking3         0.0733945    0.06422018      0.03517988         NA 0.009174312 0.009174312              NA
#head_trauma0     0.8165138    0.87155963     -0.14221364         NA 0.055045872 0.055045872              NA
#head_trauma1     0.1834862    0.12844037      0.14221364         NA 0.055045872 0.055045872              NA

# Matching
cross.out1 <- matchit(GRS_above_med ~ age + alcohol1 + smoking + head_trauma, data = meta_sub,
                 method = "full", distance = "glm", link="probit")

summary(cross.out1)
```

## Differential methylation analysis

Will used limma on all EPIC probes passing QC, modeling the data with M-values. I'll continue with this approach and transform results back to beta values later for plotting and interpretation purposes.

First, as Will did, I'll apply the updated models to (1) the cross-sex sample, (2) males, (3) females, (4) PD cases, and (5) controls. This permits us to detect whether GRS associations with DNAm are dependent on sex and/or disease status.

```{r prs ewas, eval=F}
####### Cross-sex PRS EWAS
# limma design matrix and linear model fit
design_prs <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + PD + head_trauma + smoking + alcohol1, data = meta_matched)
prs_fit <- lmFit(mvals, design_prs, weights=meta_matched$weights)
prs_fit <- eBayes(prs_fit)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

prs_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
prs_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(prs_res[abs(prs_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & prs_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0
#### logFC column is the model coefficient

####### Cases only
design_prs_case <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + head_trauma + smoking + alcohol1, data = meta_matched[meta_matched$PD=="1",])
prs_fit_case <- lmFit(mvals[,match(unlist(meta_matched[meta_sub$PD=="1","patient"]), colnames(mvals))], design_prs_case, weights=meta_matched[meta_matched$PD=="1","weights"])
prs_fit_case <- eBayes(prs_fit_case)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit_case$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

case_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit_case, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
case_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(case_res[abs(case_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & case_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0

# Controls only
design_prs_control <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + head_trauma + alcohol1 + smoking, data = meta_matched[meta_matched$PD=="0",])
prs_fit_control <- lmFit(mvals[,match(unlist(meta_matched[meta_matched$PD=="0","patient"]), colnames(mvals))], design_prs_control, weight=meta_matched[meta_matched$PD=="0","weights"])
prs_fit_control <- eBayes(prs_fit_control)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit_control$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

control_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit_control, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
control_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(control_res[abs(control_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & control_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #44

# Males
design_prs_male <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + PD + smoking + alcohol1 + head_trauma, data = meta_M_matched)
prs_fit_male <- lmFit(mvals[,match(unlist(meta_M_matched[,"patient"]), colnames(mvals_M))], design_prs_male, weights=meta_M_matched$weights)
# Coefficients not estimable: plate6 plate9 
# Partial NA coefficients for 803777 probe(s)
prs_fit_male <- eBayes(prs_fit_male)
# Estimation of var.prior failed - set to default value
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit_male$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

male_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit_male, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals_M))
male_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(male_res[abs(male_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & male_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0

# Females
design_prs_female <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + PD + smoking + alcohol1 + head_trauma, data = meta_F_matched)
prs_fit_female <- lmFit(mvals[,match(unlist(meta_F_matched[,"patient"]), colnames(mvals_F))], design_prs_female, weights=meta_F_matched$weights)
prs_fit_female <- eBayes(prs_fit_female)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit_female$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

female_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit_female, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
female_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(female_res[abs(female_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & female_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0

# PD status EWAS check
design_pd <- model.matrix(~ 1 + PD + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + smoking + head_trauma + alcohol1, data = meta_matched)
pd_fit <- lmFit(mvals, design_pd)
pd_fit <- eBayes(pd_fit)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
pd_fit_coef <- pd_fit$coefficients
m0_eff <- pd_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + pd_fit_coef[, "PD1"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

pd_res <- limma::topTable(pd_fit, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
pd_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(pd_res[abs(pd_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & pd_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0

# save everything
# put limma results in separate csv's and together as one RData object for ease later
#save(mvals, file="~/PD_GRS/TERRE_Mvals.RData")
#write.csv(meta_sub, file="~/PD_GRS/meta_for_GRS_EWAS.csv", row.names=F)
save(pd_res, prs_res, control_res, case_res, male_res, female_res, file="~/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/EWAS_limma_all_1Dec25.RData")
write.csv(pd_res, file="~/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/EWAS_PD_1Dec25.csv", row.names=F)
write.csv(prs_res, file="~/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/EWAS_GRS_cross_sex_1Dec25.csv", row.names=F)
```

Thresholds: adjusted delta beta > 0.03 (exceeding RMSE of technical replicates), FDR < 0.05.

## Differential methylation analysis with covariate adjustment, without propensity weighting

```{r prs ewas no cov, eval=F}
####### Cross-sex PRS EWAS
# limma design matrix and linear model fit
design_prs <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + PD + head_trauma + smoking + alcohol1, data = meta_matched)
prs_fit <- lmFit(mvals, design_prs)
prs_fit <- eBayes(prs_fit)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

prs_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
prs_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(prs_res[abs(prs_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & prs_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0
#### logFC column is the model coefficient
```

## Summary and next steps

When SNPs that did not pass QC in the Nalls 2019 analysis were removed from the GRS, associations with DNAm were eliminated or dampened. No models, regardless of sex or disease stratification, had any CpGs passing M-value and adjusted p-value cutoffs. This suggested the SNPs in the GRS had little influence on DNAm compared with sex and exposures, which were correlated with DNAm PCs.


Sample breakdown:

218 total

71 PD cases

147 controls

100 females

118 males
